haiku-low.q1: MySQL users row and its outbox row commit in one MySQL transaction. Postgres is updated later by the relay. A Postgres failure does not fail the caller's request.
haiku-low.q2: Only when no tombstone exists for that id and the stored version is lower than the incoming version. Otherwise never.
haiku-low.q3: Every pod reports R1 for 10 minutes, and the relay has oldest outbox age under 60 s for the last hour. Then the operator sets backfill_enabled. Read-flag skew is at most 30 s.
haiku-low.q4: One backfill replica, batches of 2000 rows. Before each batch, it checks replica lag and pauses if lag exceeds 5 s or the reading is over 10 s old.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: backfill complete, then a full comparator pass with zero mismatches and an empty outbox at its start, then the 1/10/50/100% ramp and 72 h at 100%. Source switch: 4.3 met, clean recent pass, outbox under 5 s old, normal lag, sequence exists, rollback owner on call.
haiku-low.q6: The MySQL outbox row, written in the same transaction, records it. The relay retries with backoff from 1 s to 5 min until it applies the row. Rows are never dead-lettered.
haiku-low.q7: Every copy takes a per-id lock and checks the tombstone table before applying the version rule. Deletes write tombstones that are kept forever.
haiku-low.q8: last_id lives in Postgres user_backfill_state, committed in the same transaction as each batch's rows. A crash resumes after the last commit. It stops when a batch returns empty and sets completed_at, or when the lease is lost.
haiku-low.q9: The users-compare worker checks 2000-id ranges by count and hash, then re-reads mismatches from the MySQL primary. Confirmed mismatches get an outbox upsert for repair. A Postgres-only row becomes a delete plus tombstone with a high-severity alert. Any non-zero count alerts.
haiku-low.q10: Writes take FOR SHARE on the MySQL control row, and the switch takes FOR UPDATE, so no instance can write under the other order. If the drain passes 60 s, the switch sets paused=0 and bumps epoch. Total pause budget is 90 s.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres assigns ids after the switch, with its sequence set to the max of Postgres max id and MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT while paused. Reverse mirror writes Postgres rows to MySQL with explicit ids, so no rollback sequence step is needed.
haiku-low.q12: The reverse mirror keeps MySQL current with explicit ids and version guards. Rollback repeats the pause/drain steps with source=mysql and aborts if the drain exceeds 60 s. The option ends at the S2 Postgres-only switch, no sooner than 14 days after S1 with zero reverse mismatches, and at 7.3.

sonnet.q1: The document describes no MySQL-first then Postgres write with a caller-visible Postgres failure. MySQL (users row plus outbox row) is written in one transaction. A relay applies it to Postgres afterwards, asynchronously. A Postgres failure is never seen by the caller: the write path never touches Postgres or Redis, and the relay retries with backoff.
sonnet.q2: Only if the stored version is lower than the incoming version (and, for inserts, no tombstone exists). Never otherwise.
sonnet.q3: Gate G1: every pod reports release R1 on the deploy-version metric for at least 10 minutes, and the relay has run with oldest-outbox age under 60 s for the last hour. Then the operator sets users.backfill_enabled. After a flag change, instances can disagree for up to 30 s.
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica, not the primary, in batches of 2000 rows. Before every batch it checks replica lag (mysql_replica_lag_seconds). If lag is above 5 s, or the reading is over 10 s old, it sleeps 1 s and rechecks, exporting backfill_paused_lag. It runs as a single replica with a lease.
sonnet.q5: Reads: backfill complete (2.2) and a full comparator pass that started after that, with the outbox empty at its start, finishes with zero mismatches found (Gate G2). Then a ramp of 1%, 10%, 50%, 100%, with per-step gates. Source of truth: 4.3 satisfied (72 hours at 100% with no mismatches, no outbox row older than 5 min), latest full comparator pass clean and finished after the flag hit 100, oldest outbox row under 5 s, normal replica lag, the Postgres identity sequence exists, and a rollback owner on call.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row in MySQL (user_sync_outbox), written in the same transaction as the users write, records it. The relay worker retries with backoff, and the row stays until applied. The comparator also finds differences and queues repairs.
sonnet.q7: Every copy takes a per-id lock and checks the tombstone table before applying the version rule. Deletes insert a tombstone (kept forever), so a copy will not insert a row when a tombstone exists.
sonnet.q8: The cursor (last_id) is in Postgres in user_backfill_state. It is committed in the same Postgres transaction as the batch, so a crash after the commit resumes after the batch, and a crash before it redoes the batch, which is harmless thanks to the version rule. It stops when a batch query returns no rows, then it sets completed_at.
sonnet.q9: The comparator users-compare. It compares 2000-id ranges using counts and hashes, skips ids with a pending outbox row, and re-reads mismatched ids from the primary. A confirmed mismatch gets an outbox upsert row in MySQL, so the relay repairs it. A Postgres row with no MySQL row and no tombstone is turned into a delete plus tombstone, with a high-severity alert. Every mismatch is counted, and any non-zero count is an alert.
sonnet.q10: A MySQL control row (user_store_control). Every write reads it FOR SHARE in its transaction. The switch takes it FOR UPDATE, which waits for in-flight writes and blocks new ones (new writes get a retryable 503). Flags are not used because they can disagree for 30 s. If the drain is not done by t0+60 s, or the lock is not taken within 5 s, it sets paused=0 with epoch+1, stays on the old source, alerts and aborts. No data is lost. The total pause budget is 90 s.
sonnet.q11: Postgres assigns ids through its identity sequence. At the switch, with writes paused, the sequence is set to the greater of the Postgres max id and the MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT. During the reverse-mirror window, Postgres-created rows are mirrored to MySQL with explicit ids, which keeps the MySQL counter above every Postgres id. So a rollback needs no sequence step.
sonnet.q12: A reverse mirror (Postgres outbox, reverse relay with a version guard, MySQL tombstones) plus a reverse comparator keep MySQL current. Rollback uses the same procedure as 5.2 to 5.6 with source='mysql': pause, drain the reverse outbox (abort and stay on Postgres if over 60 s), flip. Pause is at most 90 s. The window is at least 14 days. The option ends at 7.2/7.3 (S2, pg_only), which is the point of no return. It cannot happen sooner than 14 days after S1, and it also needs zero reverse-comparator mismatches.
